zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Fairmount Section, Prospect Ave High-Rise Corridor, Central Main St & Courthouse District, First Ward & South Hackensack Border
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 3.785%, with an equalization ratio of 65.4%.
Public education represents 51.4% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 36.8%.
Average residential assessment is $304,110, producing an average annual tax bill of $11,510.56.

neighborhoods.name: Fairmount Section
neighborhoods.character: Historic residential neighborhood with stately colonials, Victorians, and tree-lined streets near Fairmount train station
neighborhoods.description: Historic residential crown of Hackensack featuring architectural homes, direct commuter rail to Hoboken/NYC, and local parks.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Key residential ratable anchor supporting Bergen County seat municipal services.

neighborhoods.name: Prospect Ave High-Rise Corridor
neighborhoods.character: Prestigious luxury high-rise condominium and co-op corridor adjacent to Hackensack Meridian Health University Medical Center
neighborhoods.description: Prominent luxury condo corridor offering doorman high-rises, Manhattan skyline views, and walkable access to NJ's top medical center.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High ratable density with minimal school-age child impact on Hackensack Public Schools.

neighborhoods.name: Central Main St & Courthouse District
neighborhoods.character: Bergen County government hub, historic courthouse, downtown redevelopment lofts, and commercial restaurants
neighborhoods.description: Undergoing major transit-oriented mixed-use redevelopment with thousands of luxury apartments revitalizing Main Street.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Significant PILOT redevelopment projects shifting local infrastructure service burdens.

neighborhoods.name: First Ward & South Hackensack Border
neighborhoods.character: Working-class residential neighborhood with single-family cape cods, duplexes, and local community parks
neighborhoods.description: Historic residential neighborhood convenient to Route 80, local transit buses, and Hackensack High School.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Sensitive to composite tax increases; relies heavily on state school aid formula funding.

equityAnalysis.summary: Hackensack City maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Hackensack City, homeowners pay an average of $11,510.56 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 14.14% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 65.4%, assessed values average ~65.4% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 51.4% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 36.8%, and Bergen County claims 11.8%.
